newsitem.title: USA: Ludwig should not have been at DNC meeting-Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Ludwig should not have been at DNC meeting-Clinton.

text.p: President Clinton said U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig should not have attended a White House coffee meeting for bankers last year that was hosted by Clinton and organized by the Democratic National Committee.
"In retrospect, since the DNC sponsored it I do not think the (Comptroller) of the currency should have been there," Clinton told a news conference at the White House.
Clinton said he thought it was okay for himself to meet with bankers, but that a U.S. regulator should not have attended a coffee sponsored by the Democratic party.

"I think it is an appropriate thing and can be a good thing for the President and for the Secretary of the Treasury to meet with a group of bankers and listen to them and listen to their concerns and if they have certain issues, to explore those issues," he said. "I can tell you categorically that no decision ever came out of any of those coffees where I or anyone else said this person is a contributor of ours, do what they ask us to do," he said.
Clinton was responding to reports about the May 1996 coffee meeting that said several bankers present subsequently made significant politial contributions to the Democratic party.

The chairman of a House banking subcommittee on oversight and investigations, Rep. Spencer Bachus of Alabama, wrote to Ludwig asking for information about what transpired at the White House meeting and whether there had been others like it.
"I know you share my view that even the mere appearance of political influence being exerted on the bank regulatory process should be scrupulously avoided," Bachus said in his letter to Ludwig.
